provider_query: Hacker News discussion of SQLite as an application file format
answer:
Relevant Hacker News threads on SQLite as an application file format (official essay: [sqlite.org/appfileformat.html](https://sqlite.org/appfileformat.html)):

1. **[SQLite as an Application File Format](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=46076642)** — ~178 points, ~99 comments. Direct discussion of the SQLite essay. Includes the Mapbox MBTiles origin story (bundling many small map tiles into one SQLite file) and debate over tree-shaped documents vs flat tables. [[1]](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=46076642)

2. **[What If OpenDocument Used SQLite?](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=45132498)** — ~279 points, Sept 2025, ~105 comments. Practical caveats if you ship SQLite documents: `secure_delete`, hardening for untrusted files, and SQLite’s stance that opening untrusted DBs is a niche case. Also notes the ~2 GiB BLOB limit. [[2]](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=45132498)

3. **[“The killer feature… is as an application file format”](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=40655974)** — Comment thread citing the essay. Praises incremental updates vs ZIP-style bundles; cites Audacity project files and a game system where artists edited content with ordinary DB tools. [[3]](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=40655974)

4. **[Apple `.car` format thread (gzipped JSON vs SQLite)](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47046185)** — Argues binary blobs belong in SQLite rather than Base64-in-JSON. Examples: Firefox favicons, iOS photos, Kodi, Visual C++ browsing data; Audacity again as a crash-safe streaming project file. [[4]](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47046185)

5. **[SQLite as an app format vs an interchange format](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=39797104)** — SQLite is strong for one app’s documents but a weak generic interchange format because readers must embed SQLite. Discusses Application ID at header offset 68 so `file(1)` can tell formats apart. [[5]](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=39797104)

6. **[Tree data vs tables (same essay thread)](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=46080273)** — If the document is a tree, SQLite is less obvious unless you normalize with foreign keys or mix JSON blobs with binary rows; still preferred over ZIP for mixed content. [[6]](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=46080273)

7. **[Schema makes the file self-describing (2021)](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=26163589)** — Argument that the on-disk schema (plain text in the file) is what makes SQLite a real application format, not just an engine bolted onto a blob. [[7]](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=26163589)

8. **[Tangent: SQLite instead of ELF](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=46079326)** — On the essay thread, a side discussion of storing/querying executables via SQLite (sqlelf), distinct from document file formats but sparked by the same post. [[8]](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=46079326)

### 2025

My hunch is that existing LLMs make it easier to build a new programming language in a way that captures new developers.

Most programming languages are similar enough to existing languages that you only need to know a small number of details to use them: what's the core syntax for variables, loops, conditionals and functions? How does memory management work? What's the concurrency model? [...] The university of Paris went from something like 13 institutes to maybe one to then a bunch more. Someone will suggest modelling to solve this but here lies the biggest problem:

The correct modelling depends on the questions you want to answer.

results.title: YAVCHN
results.snippet:
Well, that's not the whole story. Whenever I browse Hacker News, I open the discussion in a new tab, click through to the article from there, pop back to the discussion, and so on, until I've got more tabs open than I can keep track of. What I really want is a quick look at the article and a sense of whether there's any interesting discussion, before I dive into either one.

## Three panes [...] ## Three panes

YAVCHN, short for Yet Another Vibe-Coded Hacker News, puts everything on one screen. The stories are listed down the left. The top right shows the linked article in a clean reader mode, and the bottom right shows the discussion. You can read Lobsters in it as well as Hacker News.

It follows the same rules I try to follow everywhere else: [...] Windowed Classic
